newsitem.title: UK: ONS TO CHANGE BASIS OF UK NATIONAL ACCOUNTS.
newsitem.headline: ONS TO CHANGE BASIS OF UK NATIONAL ACCOUNTS.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics plans to change the basis for UK national accounts and balance of payments figures to bring them into line with updated international standards, it announced on Friday.
The changes will not take effect until autumn 1998 and will be introduced at the same time as the five-yearly rebasing of economic growth figures, with 1995 replacing 1990 as the base year.
An expanded business register, used as the basis for many of the ONS's surveys, will also kick in at the same time.
"There will inevitably be some impact on growth rates but it wouldn't be expected to have a very big effect," an ONS statistician said.
The changes will make international comparisions easier but the UK is also obliged by the EU to make the changes for administrative reasons.

There will be an impact on quarterly data releases and the annual "Blue Book" which covers national accounts and the "Pink Book" which covers balance of payments. The Blue and Pink books for 1997 were published today and will appear in a different form next year, heralding the introduction of the changes.

The main change to the Balance of Payments series is a new definition of the UK to exclude the Channel Islands and the Isle of Man. This means that payments by British banks to offshore accounts in these locations, which are not part of the EU, will now show up in trade figures.
The main changes are as follows:
A new accounting structure
-- The ONS will publish production accounts for various sectors of the economy.
Changes to the definitions of major aggregates:
-- gross domestic product

-- Recategorisation of some types of expenditure from current to capital accounts eg dairy cows because their output is continual whereas beef cows stay in the current sector because theirs is limited.
Mineral explorations, computer software and artistic originals to be included within capital formation.
New terminology
-- "inventories" to replace "stocks"
-- "rest of the world" to replace "overseas"
New classifications
-- expanded sector detail including more infomration on the financial sector and creation of new insurance sector.
-- new classification of financial instruments.
